claims.text: In Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C, formation and persistence of a stable, coherent protective oxide are governed by selective oxidation of Al and, secondarily, Cr.
Al diffuses outward and forms an externally continuous Al2O3 scale.
High oxygen activity in air accelerates Al consumption relative to vacuum exposure.
Air exposure produces a thicker duplex Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale and a deeper Al-depleted region.
Al depletion caused by oxidation promotes transformation of the underlying BCC/B2 microstructure.
Low-oxygen vacuum exposure slows oxidation and limits both Al depletion and oxide growth.
Vacuum exposure produces a thin, predominantly alumina-based protective film.
The nominally equiatomic as-cast AlCrCoFeNi alloy consists mainly of approximately 79% BCC and 21% B2.
The initial alloy has a fine spinodally decomposed microstructure.
The initial alloy has slightly less Al than its nominal composition.
Oxidation becomes pronounced above 900 °C under the specified heating conditions.
Oxidation induces transformation of the initial BCC/B2 substrate into intermediate FCC and Cr-Fe-rich sigma phases at moderate temperatures.
Al depletion destabilizes the substrate and reinforces selective oxidation and scale thickening.
Rapid oxidation in air forms an externally continuous Al2O3 scale associated with an inner Cr2O3 layer.
Relative to air-exposed samples, vacuum-exposed samples will have a much thinner oxide scale, less Al depletion, and less subsurface phase alteration.
The as-cast polished room-temperature alloy has no thermally grown oxide scale.
The proposed mechanism may extend from X = Al alloys to analogous X = Si or Mn CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Threshold temperatures and Al-depletion kinetics vary with minor compositional fluctuations and processing history.
